FACULTY SENATE OFFICE 224 PASTORE HALL, 51 LOWER COLLEGE ROAD, KINGSTON, RI 02881 USA, P: 401.874.2616 Faculty Senate Resolution 2024-2025-01 Faculty Senate Meeting of December 12, 2024 Resolution of Appreciation and Gratitude Honoring the Estate Gift from Alumna Helen Izzi Schilling WHEREAS, Helen Izzi Schilling, a distinguished alumna of the University of Rhode Island, Class of 1954, and her late husband, Francis Schilling, have made a profound and lasting impact on the University through a historic estate gift of $65 million, the largest philanthropic contribution in the history of the University of Rhode Island; and WHEREAS, the gift establishes the Helen Izzi Schilling ’54 and Francis Schilling Scholars Program, an endowed scholarship that will provide significant financial support—up to $20,000 per year for four years—to high-achieving undergraduate students pursuing degrees in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields; and WHEREAS, this transformative scholarship program not only offers financial aid but also leadership development and mentoring, empowering students to achieve their academic and professional goals, and ensuring the future success of the University’s students in vital and innovative disciplines; and WHEREAS, Helen Izzi Schilling’s education in the sciences, which began at URI, laid the foundation for a distinguished career as a registered dietitian, educator, and businesswoman, making a significant impact on the healthcare community over five decades; and WHEREAS, Helen Izzi Schilling was deeply committed to the University and to making a difference in the lives of students, particularly those who, like her, sought careers in service to others; and WHEREAS, Francis Schilling, after completing his M.B.A. and pursuing a successful career in industry, including as vice president at GE Medical Systems, introduced pioneering medical technologies such as CT and MRI scanners to healthcare providers, demonstrating his commitment to innovation and progress; and WHEREAS, the Schilling’s extraordinary generosity is a testament to their unwavering belief in the power of education, their dedication to advancing STEM fields, and their desire to leave a legacy that will inspire future generations of students; and

WHEREAS, the Schilling’s gift further strengthens the University’s mission of providing transformative educational opportunities, adding to the momentum of URI’s recently completed comprehensive campaign, which raised over $73 million for financial aid; and WHEREAS, the Schilling family’s deep ties to Rhode Island, dating back to the early 1900s, and their ongoing commitment to the state’s future, underscore the lasting impact of their support for the University and its students; WHEREAS, the faculty will enjoy the benefits and are ready to join in force to support the development of the scores of students who will benefit from this award far into the future, WHEREAS, collaborative work with their son, Paul Schilling, with past URI President Robert Carothers, current University of Rhode Island President Marc Parlange, and the University of Rhode Island Foundation & Alumni Engagement President Lil O’Rourke fashioned this historic arrangement to benefit high achieving students in concrete and direct ways, WHEREAS, the opportunity for life-changing support for strong students from all walks of life, including those with immigration heritages such as that of Helen Izzi Schilling herself, connotes deep concern, empathy, and intergenerational support for unknown others, NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Faculty Senate of the University of Rhode Island, on behalf of the entire University community, expresses its profound appreciation and heartfelt gratitude to the Schilling Family and the memories of Helen Izzi Schilling and Francis Schilling for their visionary generosity, their enduring legacy of support for URI students, and their commitment to ensuring that future generations have the tools and resources they need to achieve their highest ambitions; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution be entered into the official minutes of the Faculty Senate and that a copy be sent to the Schilling family as a token of our deep appreciation.

Unanimously adopted this 12th day of December, 2024.
Theodore Walls, URI Faculty Senate President

The environmental and natural resource economics major integrates the natural sciences with economics to help us understand why many of earth’s natural resources are under threat and how we can design policies to address these threats.
This major teaches students to weigh options and make important decisions concerning the protection, restoration, development, and use of our natural resources.
The major prepares students for graduate school or for careers in the public and private sector that address environmental and natural resource management, business, or public policy.

Graduates gain an understanding of both natural sciences and the economy.
The degree requires a minimum of 120 credits, including 24 credits in concentration.
In addition to satisfying the general education requirements, students need nine credits in introductory professional courses, including natural resource conservation (NRS 100), introduction to resource economics (EEC 105), and environmental economics and policy (EEC 205).
The major also requires a minimum of three credits in written communication skills (WRT) at the 200 level or higher.
It is also possible to earn a double degree in environmental economics and general business, which we call Green Business (see details below).
